direct_answer: Aker BP states that it does not have a climate transition plan in line with ESRS requirements, because it has no targets to reduce Scope 3 emissions and it also has no timeline for if/when it will develop such a plan [Source 1]. Therefore, a 1.5°C-aligned transition plan is not disclosed/existing under ESRS E1-1, and the company does not explain how a transition plan’s targets would be compatible with limiting warming to 1.5°C [Source 1]. (While Aker BP acknowledges the Paris Agreement’s 1.5°C goal [Source 2] and uses a 1.5°C-aligned IEA NZE scenario in scenario analysis [Sources 3, 6], this is not presented as an ESRS-compliant transition plan nor as evidence that a transition plan is 1.5°C aligned [Source 1].)
compliance_rationale: ESRS E1-1 requires disclosure of whether a transition plan exists and, if it exists, how targets are compatible with 1.5°C; Aker BP explicitly states it does not have a climate transition plan in line with ESRS requirements and has no timeline to develop one [Source 1]. As a result, there is no disclosed 1.5°C alignment of a transition plan under ESRS E1-1 [Source 1].
disclosure_gaps: No ESRS-compliant climate transition plan disclosed (company explicitly states it does not have one) [Source 1].
No timeline for adoption of an ESRS-compliant transition plan [Source 1].
No explanation of how the undertaking’s GHG emission reduction targets are compatible with limiting warming to 1.5°C within a transition plan context [Source 1].

No transition plan elements evidenced in the provided passages: decarbonisation levers and key actions, investments and funding, locked-in emissions assessment within the plan, governance approval, embedding in strategy/financial planning, and progress tracking (not provided; company states plan not ESRS-aligned) [Source 1].
No Scope 3 emissions reduction targets (explicitly stated), which the company links to the absence of an ESRS-aligned transition plan [Source 1].
key_findings: Aker BP states it does not have a climate transition plan in line with ESRS requirements and has no timeline to develop one [Source 1].
Aker BP acknowledges the Paris Agreement and the goal to limit warming to 1.5°C [Source 2].
Aker BP uses IEA World Energy Outlook scenarios including the NZE scenario described as a 1.5°C pathway for scenario analysis, but this is not disclosed as a transition plan [Sources 3, 6].
